cs.t: Victorinox swiss army knife circa 2007 ish. Broke into my old flat with it once. Billingham 550 camera bag I bought in 1992 for £150. Brilliant. Pilot Capless pen from 2013. Hundreds of miles of handwriting. About £130
cs.th: Ask HN: What are some of your “buy it for life” purchases?

cs.t: victorinox minichamp or midnight minichamp. It covers about five of the items listed in the comments. Pen ,light ,lockpick ,bottle opener, knife...

1. Apple iPhone 4 and newer (hardware & software) 2. Commodore 64 (greatest desktop PC design for many reasons from hardware, software and documentation) 3. Apple Macbook Pro 2016 and all unibody MBPs (hardware) I also really like my Victorinox Waiter Swiss Army Knife. The corkscrew is better than on my Leatherman and I use these at least once a week as we take a bottle of wine out to dinner.
cs.th: Ask HN: What're the best-designed things you've ever used?

cs.t: Victorinox Farmer - just the tools I need without the heft of a multitool. A close second is the Victorinox Lumberjack. If I remember correctly it is/was the smallest SAK with a saw, which I use for all kinds of things.
cs.th: Ask HN: What is your favorite pocket knife?

cs.t: I put my Victorinox in the dishwasher with no ill effect. The biggest danger is when a visitor decides to chop a tomoto on a ceramic plate. It's no Japanese chef knife, but a bargin for what it is.
